thread:
amelia: Heads-up — I noticed a couple of broken quickstart snippets during new hire onboarding today.
amelia: The README uses a multiline curl with backslashes which breaks in PowerShell and some CI runners. Also the examples use `REDWOOD_KEY` as the env var but libs expect `REDWOOD_API_KEY`.
amelia: Broken curl from README:
```
curl \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{\"input\":\"hi\"}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
amelia: Paste that into PowerShell and you get `curl: (6) Could not resolve host: -H` or it treats backslashes literally.
tony: Thanks for catching. Two quick fixes: switch examples to a single-line curl (or wrap in bash/zsh block) and add a PowerShell snippet using Invoke-RestMethod.
tony: Example fixes I'll add:
Single-line curl:
```
curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d '{\"input\":\"hi\"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
PowerShell (Invoke-RestMethod):
```
$headers = @{ Authorization = \"Bearer $env:REDWOOD_API_KEY\"; \"Content-Type\" = \"application/json\" }
Invoke-RestMethod -Uri https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -Method Post -Headers $headers -Body '{\"input\":\"hi\"}'
```
harper: Also the TypeScript example in docs uses a default import which fails for folks with esModuleInterop off. Current README: `import RedwoodClient from '@redwood/inference'` — that bombs in strict TS configs.
harper: I'll update examples to show both patterns and a short note: `// If you use \"esModuleInterop\": true use default import, otherwise use named import` and provide `import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'` plus a tiny Node smoke script under docs/examples that reads process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY.
\amalia: (typo) I meant amelia: Can we also make the sample app in examples/quickstart use the same env var? We have a couple of repos where Python uses REDWOOD_API and JS uses REDWOOD_KEY — churn city for new users.
docs-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/651 — normalizes env var to REDWOOD_API_KEY, updates curl/PowerShell examples, adds TS import note, updates examples/quickstart.
zoe: Nice. Can we add a docs CI step that runs the quickstart smoke script? Even a non-networked dry-run that validates syntax and env variable usage would catch copy/paste regressions.
tony: Good call. I'll add a lightweight Node smoke test that requires REDWOOD_API_KEY to be set in CI and runs `node docs/examples/quickstart-smoke.js`. For offline checks I'll add a lint script that ensures the README examples use the canonical env var name.
harper: Filing follow-up issue to sweep other language docs (python, go, ruby) for parity: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/219
amelia: Thanks folks — once the PR lands I'll run through the onboarding checklist and update the new-hire guide with the platform notes. :thumbsup:
